questions.question: What is the expected major product when Phenylmagnesium bromide (PhMgBr) is treated with 1. Solid CO2 (dry ice); 2. Aqueous HCl?
questions.explanation: Treating Phenylmagnesium bromide (PhMgBr) with 1. Solid CO2 (dry ice); 2. Aqueous HCl yields Benzoic acid (PhCOOH). Rationale: Grignard reagent attacks electrophilic carbon of CO2; acidification yields carboxylic acid with 1 added carbon.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Phenylacetonitrile (PhCH2CN) into Phenylacetic acid (PhCH2COOH) + Ammonium sulfate?
questions.explanation: To convert Phenylacetonitrile (PhCH2CN) into Phenylacetic acid (PhCH2COOH) + Ammonium sulfate, the appropriate reagent is Aqueous H2SO4 / heat. Rationale: Nitrile is protonated and hydrated stepwise through primary amide to carboxylic acid.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzonitrile (PhCN) is treated with 1. Aqueous NaOH / heat; 2. Aqueous HCl?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzonitrile (PhCN) with 1. Aqueous NaOH / heat; 2. Aqueous HCl yields Benzoic acid (PhCOOH) + NH3. Rationale: Hydroxide attacks the cyano carbon; subsequent acidification isolates the free carboxylic acid.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Butanenitrile (CH3CH2CH2CN) into 1-Butanamine (CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2)?
questions.explanation: To convert Butanenitrile (CH3CH2CH2CN) into 1-Butanamine (CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2), the appropriate reagent is 1. LiAlH4 in ether; 2. H2O. Rationale: Lithium aluminum hydride delivers two hydrides to the nitrile carbon, yielding a primary alkylamine.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzonitrile (PhCN) is treated with 1. DIBAL-H in toluene (-78°C); 2. Aqueous H3O+?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzonitrile (PhCN) with 1. DIBAL-H in toluene (-78°C); 2. Aqueous H3O+ yields Benzaldehyde (PhCHO). Rationale: DIBAL-H at -78°C transfers a single hydride, forming an imine intermediate hydrolyzed to an aldehyde.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzonitrile (PhCN) into Acetophenone (PhCOCH3)?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzonitrile (PhCN) into Acetophenone (PhCOCH3), the appropriate reagent is 1. Methylmagnesium bromide (CH3MgBr); 2. H3O+. Rationale: Grignard adds once to nitrile forming an imine magnesium salt; aqueous acid hydrolysis yields a ketone.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Mild heat (50°C) to yield Acetone (CH3COCH3) + CO2 gas as the major product?
questions.explanation: Acetoacetic acid (CH3COCH2COOH) reacts with Mild heat (50°C) to yield Acetone (CH3COCH3) + CO2 gas. Rationale: Six-membered cyclic transition state transfers the carboxyl proton to carbonyl oxygen, expelling CO2.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Methylmalonic acid (CH3CH(COOH)2) is treated with Heat (150°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating Methylmalonic acid (CH3CH(COOH)2) with Heat (150°C) yields Propanoic acid (CH3CH2COOH) + CO2 gas. Rationale: Heating dicarboxylic acids with two carboxyls on the same carbon triggers decarboxylation to monocarboxylic acid.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Thionyl chloride (SOCl2) / heat to yield Benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) + SO2 + HCl as the major product?
questions.explanation: Benzoic acid (PhCOOH) reacts with Thionyl chloride (SOCl2) / heat to yield Benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) + SO2 + HCl. Rationale: Conversion of carboxyl hydroxyl into chlorosulfite allows nucleophilic chloride displacement.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzoic acid (PhCOOH) is treated with Ethanol (excess) / concentrated H2SO4?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzoic acid (PhCOOH) with Ethanol (excess) / concentrated H2SO4 yields Ethyl benzoate + H2O. Rationale: Acid-catalyzed nucleophilic acyl substitution of carboxylic acid with alcohol under equilibrium conditions.
